classification.difficultyReason: Identify each plot’s overall direction and judge scatter about a straight line, including distinguishing a weak negative trend from stronger trends.

content.prompt: For each scatterplot, state the direction (positive or negative) and strength (strong, moderate or weak) of the correlation.

spec.description: Nine visible observations, including three near 17–19 hours; coordinates estimated from the printed grid.
spec.mathematics: Time 0–40 hours, grid step 5; mark 0–90%, grid step 10. All printed tick labels retained.

answer.worked: Marks generally increase with time. The points cluster fairly closely around an upward-sloping straight line, indicating strong positive correlation; moderate positive correlation is also acceptable by eye.

spec.description: Twelve observations with repeated ages 3, 4, 6 and 7; non-integer prices estimated from the printed grid.
spec.mathematics: Age 0–8 years, grid step 1 with even-numbered labels; price 0–9 thousand dollars, grid step 1.

answer.worked: Prices generally decrease as age increases. The downward trend is clear, with some scatter; strong or moderate negative correlation is acceptable by eye.

spec.description: Broad descending cloud. Temperature positions after the axis break represent the printed 20–40 scale; the left origin label 0 is retained without treating the intervening range as continuous. Coordinates are visually estimated.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal grid step 2.5°C after the break; vertical grid step 2.5 with score labels 5, 10, 15. White rectangular masking preserves the broken-axis cue.

answer.worked: Scores tend to decrease as temperature increases, but the points are widely scattered: weak negative correlation.
